highlights:
[Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO? 5 candidates, ranked - Newsweek]

On Thursday, Nvidia's board of directors announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned after 33 years leading the company.

It thanked Huang for the “profound” contributions he made since cofounding Nvidia in 1993 and said he would be replaced on an interim basis by Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress.

…

[Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO? 5 candidates, ranked - Newsweek > 1. Ian Buck, Nvidia]

Buck joined Nvidia in 2004, and as its vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, he possesses a unique understanding of both the company’s infrastructure and the technology that has propelled it to the forefront of the semiconductor sector and of the global AI arms race. Buck is also the engineer behind CUDA, the software that allows customers to use Nvidia’s GPUs as more general-purpose engines.

As a result, he has emerged as a frontrunner—or at least a preferred candidate—in the eyes of some analysts and prediction markets.

"Ian Buck is the strongest long-term internal candidate given his role in creating CUDA and leading Nvidia's hyperscale business,” Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters.

…

Tae Kim, author of *The Nvidia Way: Jensen Huang and the Making of a Tech Giant*, called Buck “one of the most important figures in Nvidia’s history” in a blog post on Thursday. “He oversees the company’s AI hardware and software products deployed with hyperscalers and other customers. He has the engineering knowledge, experience, close data center customer relationships, and employee respect needed to lead Nvidia into its next chapter.”

Analysis from The Action Network also showed Buck leading the pack, with odds around 36 percent following Huang’s resignation.

…

[Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO? 5 candidates, ranked - Newsweek > 3. Colette Kress]

The Action Network lists her as Buck’s closest contender, and the company extolled her qualifications in Thursday’s announcement.

results.title: Nvidia executive Ian Buck emerges as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets
results.description: Prediction markets are pointing to Nvidia VP Ian Buck as a frontrunner for permanent CEO role. Published: 1 day ago

highlights:
[Nvidia executive Ian Buck emerges as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets]

With Jensen Huang out as CEO at Nvidia (NVDA) and CFO Colette Kress taking on the role of interim CEO, Wall Street, the company's partners, and its customers are waiting to find out who the next permanent CEO will be.

There are a number of candidates inside and outside of the company who could fill the position. But prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have zeroed in on Nvidia VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck as the company's next leader.

Both sites rank the odds of Buck taking over at roughly 40%.

Buck has worked at Nvidia for the last 22 years, rising from a systems engineer to his current role as the head of the company's biggest businesses.

The executive also has the kind of engineering chops that Nvidia's board may find compelling for the CEO role.

Buck has a Ph.D. from Stanford University in computer science and, more importantly, developed Nvidia's CUDA technology.

…

CUDA allows companies to use the chip giant's graphics processing units (GPUs) for general computing, a capability that was instrumental in turning Nvidia into the AI powerhouse it is today.

But Buck has a hard act to follow. Huang's charismatic personality drew customers and investors, turning him into one of the tech industry's biggest stars.

…

KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh wrote in a note to investors that Kress's appointment as interim CEO is constructive "given her tenure as CFO since 2013 and deep institutional knowledge of Nvidia's business and strategy."

Whoever Nvidia's board eventually chooses to lead the company will have plenty of questions to answer about its future and whether it can continue to dominate the industry as it did under Huang.

- Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, the Wall Street Journal reported; Nvidia fell 8.6% after hours to $158.76 (7:55 PM ET) and has no named successor.

Nvidia's (NASDAQ: NVDA) board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang and could meet as soon as Wednesday night, The Wall Street Journal reported at 5:27 PM ET, after a New York Times report that Huang had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell. Nvidia has not commented. The stock was at $158.76 in after-hours trading at 7:55 PM ET, down 8.6% from Wednesday's close and 14.9% since the November 6 close, the last before Huang admitted an affair. That is about $673 billion of market value gone in a week.

Which puts one question ahead of all the others: who runs a $3.83 trillion company that has never had any CEO but its founder? Nvidia has never named a successor. "Mr. Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place," Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson told Reuters on Wednesday. Among the people who know the company's inner workings, one name keeps coming up: Ian Buck.

…

[Meet Ian Buck: The NVIDIA Executive Insiders Believe Is the One Man Who Can Replace Jensen Huang > Who Ian Buck is]

Buck runs Nvidia's hyperscale and high-performance computing business, the part of the company that sells to the giant cloud and AI customers whose data center spending made Nvidia the most valuable chipmaker in the world. He has been at Nvidia for about two decades. Before that, as a Stanford Ph.D. student, he built Brook, one of the first programming languages for running general computing work on graphics chips. At Nvidia he became a key architect of CUDA, the software platform that lets developers write programs for Nvidia's chips.

results.title: Nvidia executive Ian Buck leads CEO succession odds at 35.5% following Huang exit
results.description: Nvidia CEO succession sees Ian Buck leading at 35.5% probability after Huang exit, amid ongoing search for a permanent chief executive.

highlights:
[Nvidia executive Ian Buck leads CEO succession odds at 35.5% following Huang exit]

Interim CEO Colette Kress follows with a 25.5% probability as Nvidia's board searches for a permanent replacement.

…

Nvidia executive Ian Buck has emerged as the leading candidate to replace Jensen Huang as the company’s permanent CEO, with a 35.5% implied probability, according to a November 12 prediction market analysis from The Action Network.

…

> “With Ian Buck leading our analysis at a 35.5% implied probability, followed by interim CEO Colette Kress at 25.5%, NVIDIA’s succession remains far from settled,” said Ben Mendelowitz, a prediction markets analyst at The Action Network.

The analysis follows Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s president, CEO and board member after 33 years leading the company. According to Nvidia’s SEC filing, the board accepted his resignation on November 11 and appointed Kress as interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones as board chair.

Nvidia confirmed the leadership transition on November 12, announcing that its board had begun searching for a permanent successor and would consider both internal and external candidates.

Mendelowitz also noted that an earlier analysis showed the implied probability of Huang leaving Nvidia jumping from 13.2% to 76.6% between November 9 and November 12.

results.title: Ian Buck built Nvidia's secret weapon. Jensen Huang's departure makes it even more essential to the company's future.
results.description: Ian Buck has spent his career building CUDA, Nvidia's most important software. Bloomberg/ Getty Images ... This story is available exclusively to Business Insider subscribers. Become an Insider and start reading now.

highlights:
[Ian Buck built Nvidia's secret weapon. Jensen Huang's departure makes it even more essential to the company's future.]

*Editor's note: This story was originally published in June of 2025, but has been updated to reflect Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Users on the* *prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket are giving* *Nvidia's Ian Buck the highest odds of permanently succeeding Huang.*

As Nvidia enters its post-Jensen Huang era, one of the people best positioned to shape its future is the engineer who helped build its moat. Ian Buck has spent more than two decades at Nvidia and created CUDA, the once-obscure software platform that has since become the foundation of the AI boom.

The 48-year-old's contribution to Nvidia is hard-coded into the company's history. He's been working alongside Huang since 2004, when he started building the company's breakthrough software, CUDA. Back then, the team had two people and two libraries. Today, CUDA supports more than 900 libraries and artificial intelligence models. Each library corresponds to an industry using Nvidia technology.

Especially in light of Huang's departure, Buck's influence is just beginning. CUDA is the platform from which Nvidia jumped to, at one point, 90% market share in AI computing. CUDA is how the company defends its moat.

…

[Ian Buck built Nvidia's secret weapon. Jensen Huang's departure makes it even more essential to the company's future. > One architecture to rule them all]

He became fixated on proving that you could use GPUs for anything and everything. He received funding from Nvidia and the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, among others, to develop tools to turn a GPU into a general-purpose supercomputing machine. When the company saw Brook—Buck's attempt at a programming language that applied the power of GPUs beyond graphics, Nvidia hired him.

…

The rise of CUDA as an essential element in the world of AI wasn't inevitable. Huang insisted on making every chip compatible with the software, even though hardly anyone was using it, despite it being free. In fact, Nvidia lost millions of dollars for more than a decade because of CUDA.

…

[Ian Buck built Nvidia's secret weapon. Jensen Huang's departure makes it even more essential to the company's future. > Ian Buck's next act]

"One of the most challenging parts of my job often is to try to predict the future, but AI is always surprising us," Buck said at a Bank of America conference in 2025. Understanding what the smartest minds in AI need from Nvidia is paramount.

…

"Everyone's trying to hire these guys, especially after DeepSeek," said Witt. "This was not a sexy domain in computer science for a long time. Now it is white hot." Huang's departure will make that side of his role even more important as several industry analysts have expressed concern that Nvidians may be more likely to leave the company now. Historically, Nvidia has had an extremely low rate of staff turnover.

…

[Ian Buck built Nvidia's secret weapon. Jensen Huang's departure makes it even more essential to the company's future. > Who's Nvidia's next CEO?]

Buck is more than a decade younger than Huang and has been part of the Huang succession discussion long before the current scandal.

…

"Jensen has three right-hand men," Tan told BI before he took over at Intel. Buck is one. Vice President of GPU Engineering Jonah Alben is another. And CFO Colette Kress, though clearly not a man, is the third, Tan said. Kress was appointed interim CEO by Nvidia's board Tuesday.

"Prediction markets have identified Rene Haas, former Nvidia VP and current CEO of Arm, as a potential external replacement, in addition to internal candidates Colette Kress and Ian Buck, head of Nvidia's AI efforts," said Brian Colello, Senior Equity Analyst at Morningstar, in an email Thursday.
